business_scope.primary_industry_name: Offshore Building Information Modeling (BIM) and Structural Drafting

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United Kingdom-Gibraltar Double Taxation Arrangement (unilateral relief applied under Gibraltar Income Tax Act 2010; no separate full DTAAP)
United Kingdom bilateral investment treaties extended to Gibraltar by Order in Council (e.g., UK-China BIT, UK-UAE BIT, UK-Qatar BIT)
Gibraltar-EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement continuity provisions applicable via the UK-EU TCA (services and digital trade access)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: The operative vehicle, notwithstanding the Bermuda Exempted Company template in the pipeline, is a Gibraltar private company limited by shares under the Companies Act 2014 (ss. 24-31 name; ss. 104-108 registered office; s. 116 annual return). Subject to: Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 (Gibraltar) Part IV; Criminal Justice Act 2015 (Gibraltar); Sanctions Act 2019 (Gibraltar); Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Act 2017 (Gibraltar) and the Beneficial Ownership Regulations; Financial Services Act 2019 (Gibraltar); and the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission AML/CFT Handbook (revised 2023), binding on all licensed corporate service providers.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (extracted from the Gibraltar Companies Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar, HM Government of Gibraltar
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) Legalisation Office (competent authority for Gibraltar-origin public documents); consular legalization required only where the destination state is not party to the Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association (notarized certified copy, including board authorization for foreign registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Gibraltar Notary Public (licensed under the Legal Profession Act 2016 (Gibraltar))
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (UK FCDO Legalisation Office) or, for non-Hague destination jurisdictions, full consular legalization chain via the destination state's embassy in London

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and Beneficial Ownership Register extract (non-public, issued for counterparty due diligence use)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar; UBO extraction limited to competent authorities and properly authorized financial institutions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via UK FCDO Legalisation Office or consular legalization in line with the specific counterparty's KYC and public procurement rules

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory layered screening against: (i) the UN Consolidated List and UN Security Council Resolutions as implemented by the Sanctions Act 2019 (Gibraltar) and UK Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering Act 2018 (extended); (ii) HM Treasury (OFSI) Consolidated List; (iii) OFAC SDN List, required for USD wire clearing and correspondent banking; (iv) Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit's domestic risk indicators; and (v) commercial PEP databases (Refinitiv World-Check or equivalent). Enhanced due diligence applies to all PEPs, senior foreign political figures, and FATF grey-listed/high-risk territorial relationships. UBO and senior management PEP status must be verified at onboarding and on an ongoing event-driven basis; CDD records retained for at least five years post-relationship under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies House Gibraltar - online incorporation and name reservation portal operated by the Registrar of Companies, HM Government of Gibraltar
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the sole official legal language of the Gibraltarian register. All approved company names must be presented in Latin script using the English alphabet; Greek, Cyrillic, CJK, and other non-Latin character strings are not recorded as the registered legal name. Trade names using foreign scripts must be accompanied by a certified English/Latin phonetic transliteration and must not create a false impression of association with a foreign state. The registered legal name must conclude with 'Limited' or 'Ltd' for this private limited company type.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection under ss. 25-28 of the Companies Act 2014, the applicant may within 21 days submit a written reconsideration request to the Registrar of Companies, attaching legal arguments and evidence of prior use or consent. If the reconsideration is refused, the applicant may file an appeal by way of judicial review in the Supreme Court of Gibraltar on an originating motion within 28 days of the Registrar's written refusal. Where the name is refused solely because of a sensitive token, the applicant may apply to the Minister of Commerce for prior ministerial consent through the Companies Registry's sensitive-name consent procedure; ministerial consent, once granted, is filed with the Registrar and clears the incorporation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is partially acceptable. The statutory registered office must be a physical street address in Gibraltar at which legal process can be served during normal business hours (ss. 104-105, Companies Act 2014). A GFSC-licensed corporate service provider commonly supplies this physical registered office together with a local company secretary. Purely virtual premises with no local management, no local books, and no accessible records will weaken the preferred territorial tax position under the Income Tax Act 2010 (Gibraltar), may trigger economic substance enquiries, and may disqualify the company from certain fee exemptions and counterparty procurement panels in civil-infrastructure and BIM/CAD outsourcing contracts.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate for the engineering-drafting outsourcing sector; estimated 8-12% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the Registrar or the GFSC where a licensed CSP is used. The likelihood rises above 20% only if the company later obtains a financial services licence or applies for a tax licence. For this non-licensed, low-risk standard tier, no routine inspection is expected during the first year if the registered office, UBO register, and local accounting records are maintained in Gibraltar.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Bermuda Companies Act 1981, as amended: Part II (Incorporation) and Part III (Exempted Companies), notably ss. 14-20 and s. 18 (exempted company filing, memorandum registration, registered office, curbs on local business); Economic Substance Act 2018 (declaration); Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966, s. 6 (tax guarantee). For the Gibraltar physical branch: Gibraltar Companies Act 2014, Part 19 (Overseas Companies).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Bermuda — 43 Church Street, Hamilton HM 12, Bermuda (incorporation); Gibraltar Companies Registry, Registrar of Companies, Government of Gibraltar (branch registration).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Bermuda: Memorandum of Association of an Exempted Company filed with the Registrar of Companies, followed by issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation; Gibraltar: Overseas Company — Place of Business Notice under the Companies Act 2014.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Bermuda Exempted Company; at least one share must be issued and fully paid (par value commonly US$1) and the Memorandum must state an authorized capital (usual minimum US$12,000). No escrow/deposit account is required by Bermuda law. In Gibraltar the overseas branch is likewise subject to no minimum capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION — [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED: The undersigned directors, acting pursuant to the Companies Act 1981 and the Articles of Association, hereby resolve: (1) the Memorandum of Association as registered be approved and the registered office and resident secretary be confirmed; (2) the subscription of shares by the initial shareholder be ratified and the statutory share register opened; (3) [name], [name], and [name] be appointed as President, Secretary, and Treasurer respectively; (4) bank and Wise mandate openings be authorized with the President and Secretary as signatories; (5) the common seal be adopted; and (6) the corporate service provider be directed to complete all statutory filings in Bermuda and Gibraltar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Pre-Clearance and Availability Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Bermuda (Ministry of Finance) — name search and reservation processed through a licensed Corporate Service Provider under the Corporate Service Provider Business Act 2001, Bermuda.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two or three proposed names in the format '... Limited' to the licensed CSP. The CSP runs a live availability search against the Bermuda Registry's index and files a formal name reservation where the desired name is available. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and must exclude words requiring consent (e.g., 'Bank', 'Trust', 'Royal'). A provisional reservation is recorded pending incorporation.
required_dossiers: Corporate service provider engagement letter
Proposed company names (primary and alternatives)
Entity type declaration (Exempted Company)
Beneficial owner identity details for registry clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected on grounds of similarity or prohibited words, the CSP submits revised secondary names without additional government fee; a refusal may be contested by a written submission to the Registrar demonstrating absence of confusion, accompanied by a statutory declaration of the intended trade.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Memorandum of Association and Exempted Status Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies (receiving authority); drafting and execution before a Bermuda notary or licensed CSP.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Association in the statutory exempted company form, containing the company name, the declaration that the company is an exempted company, the registered office in Bermuda, the authorized capital clause, and provisions stating the company shall not carry on business in Bermuda without a license (Companies Act 1981 s. 18). The subscriber(s) and first directors execute the Memorandum; each director signs a formal consent to act. Documents are dated and presented for stamping.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Association (exempted form)
Written consents of first directors
Subscriber details and share allocation schedule
Declaration of compliance with the Companies Act 1981
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The Registrar may requisition amendments for defective objects or improper declaration of exemption; the CSP re-executes and re-submits a conformed Memorandum with a cover letter, curing the query without loss of priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing, Stamp Duty Assessment and Government Fee Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies — Filing Window, Global House, 43 Church Street, Hamilton, Bermuda (or the Registrar's approved electronic filing channel).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the executed Memorandum, certified copies of director consents, and the Notice of Registered Office (pre-identified address of the resident secretary). The Registry assesses stamp duty on authorized share capital and the standard incorporation fee. Payment is made by bank draft or through the e-payment portal; the Registry then endorses the Memorandum and allocates the proposed registration number.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum of Association
Notice of Registered Office (Statutory Form)
Directors' consents (certified)
Government fee and stamp duty payment advice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is not ready for registration (outstanding fees or deficient schedules), the Registry issues a requisition notice; the CSP tenders a corrective filing with a 14-day cure period before the application is deemed withdrawn.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Certificate of Incorporation and Opening of Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: On satisfaction, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation. The licensed CSP then opens the statutory registers (members, directors, charges), prepares the common seal, holds the First Board Meeting to pass the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution, and issues the initial share certificate to the subscriber. The exempted company must maintain its registered office in Bermuda at the office of a licensed CSP and have a resident secretary.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Registered Memorandum (endorsed)
Board minute book
Share certificates and register of members
Resident secretary consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the Certificate contains a clerical error (name misspelling), the company files an application for administrative correction under the Registrar's rectification procedure with a certified copy of the board resolution and no additional fee for correction of Registry error.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Protection Undertaking and Economic Substance Declaration Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bermuda Tax Administration / Registrar of Companies (Economic Substance) — electronic filing via the Registrar.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the tax-exempt characterization, the company requests the standard undertaking under the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966, confirming no income taxes are imposed. Concurrently, the company submits the annual Economic Substance Declaration, identifying whether it carries on a 'relevant activity' (not the case for pure CAD/BIM outsourcing absent IP-holding structures) and confirming compliance with the corporate governance and substance reporting requirements of the Economic Substance Act 2018.
required_dossiers: Tax Protection undertaking application
Economic Substance Declaration form (annual)
Beneficial ownership return
Financial statements if the exempted company is obliged to file
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Tax Administration queries the economic substance status, the company files a supplemental notice with particulars of employees, premises and expenses in Bermuda to evidence nexus; failure to file attracts penalties, but rectification with paid penalty and corrected filing restores good standing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Gibraltar Overseas Company (Branch) Registration and Local Representation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry, Registrar of Companies, Government of Gibraltar — GRS e-filing portal and Registry counter.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of establishing a place of business in Gibraltar, deliver to the Gibraltar Registrar: an authenticated copy of the Bermuda Certificate of Incorporation, a certified copy of the Memorandum (translated if necessary), a list of directors and the secretary, the Bermuda registered office address, and a statement of the Gibraltar registered office and of a Gibraltar-resident person authorized to accept service. The Registry issues a Gibraltar overseas company number and records the branch in the register.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of Bermuda Certificate of Incorporation
Certified copy of Memorandum of Association
Board resolution authorizing the Gibraltar place of business
Form 'Overseas Company — Establishment of a Place of Business'
Consent of Gibraltar person authorized to accept service
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the Gibraltar Registrar issues a refusal or request for further information, the company delivers a notarized and apostilled dossier; defects in the local service address are cured by appointing a Gibraltar-licensed corporate agent and filing an amended overseas company notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Gibraltar Business Premises and Post-Registration Statutory Notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Development and Planning Commission (GDPC) and Gibraltar Income Tax Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the branch opens a physical office, obtain a development/permitted-use certificate for the commercial unit from the GDPC, notify the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service for the fire safety certificate, and register the branch with the Gibraltar Income Tax Office for payroll and corporate tax filings. As the global business is digital CAD/BIM outsourcing, there is no industrial plant permit; the branch merely secures a standard commercial occupancy compliance pack.
required_dossiers: Commercial lease or title deed for the Gibraltar office
Occupancy certificate / permitted-use letter from GDPC
DBS/reference check for the Gibraltar authorized representative
Employer registration form if any Gibraltar employees are hired
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any refusal of occupancy is cured by submitting structural plans and fire safety specifications to the GDPC Appeals Panel; provisional occupancy may be granted before final certification once the fire detection system certification is approved by the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial authority applies to the registered activity (ISIC 7110 — engineering design/CAD/BIM, an offshore intellectual service). Reference authority if an office is opened in Gibraltar: Gibraltar Development and Planning Commission (GDPC) for commercial premises; Department of the Environment and Climate Change for environmental compliance assessment.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating license or industrial manufacturing permit is mandated for digital CAD/BIM outsourced engineering services; only a standard commercial business registration and, where applicable, a Gibraltar Business License / occupancy permit for the physical office.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Gibraltar Department of the Environment and Climate Change (reference authority; if the office premises exceed de minimis refurbishment thresholds, the EIA Direction body may require screening).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category N/A: pure office/digital service use does not constitute a scheduled project under the Environmental Impact Assessment Regulations; no Full EIA Report or Initial Environmental Examination is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source discharges: zero industrial wastewater, no VOC-emitting processes, no hazardous waste streams. General compliance: Gibraltar waste segregation and municipal collection standards; WEEE disposal through licensed recyclers per UK-replicated legislation; workstations use low-energy equipment but no BAT emissions thresholds apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: fire alarm and evacuation certificate issued by the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service prior to occupation; structural load: approved building regulations sign-off for the office floor (design live load 2.5 kPa typical office); occupational health: risk assessment certified by a Gibraltar-accredited health and safety consultant, employers' liability insurance, and a clean workplace clearance from the Environmental Health Department.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar Taxation Office, Ministry of Finance, Gibraltar; official portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/taxation
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated entity, including a Bermuda Exempted Company, that opens a branch or permanent establishment, carries on trade in Gibraltar, or derives Gibraltar-source income must register for Income Tax by filing the prescribed application with the Gibraltar Taxation Office. The filing must include certified constitutional documents, a certificate of good standing or certificate of exemption from Bermuda, particulars of directors, shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners, details of the Gibraltar branch representative or registered address, and a signed declaration of the entity's central management and control location. The Commissioner issues a Gibraltar Tax Identification Number (TIN) once the application is verified. Non-resident entities with no Gibraltar permanent establishment and no Gibraltar-source income are not obliged to obtain a TIN and may alternatively request a Certificate of Non-Residence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. A Bermuda Exempted Company qualifies for tax-exempt-zone treatment by establishing and maintaining central management and control outside Gibraltar and by having no permanent establishment in Gibraltar. Qualifying Companies and Exempt Companies may nevertheless elect to be assessed under the Income Tax Act 2010 preferential categories where applicable; hybrid mismatch and ATAD anti-avoidance rules apply and may override elective characterisation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: None — Gibraltar does not operate VAT or GST; imports of goods are subject to Customs and Excise Duties, and certain local supplies may bear Purchase Duty.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: N/A — no VAT/GST threshold applies. Any person or entity importing goods into Gibraltar must register with the Gibraltar Customs and Excise Department irrespective of annual value.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, electronic invoicing mandate, or digital stamping regime applies in Gibraltar. Customs declarations must be submitted electronically through the Gibraltar Customs electronic data interchange system; services exports require no fiscal clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable because Gibraltar has no VAT/GST. Exported goods fall outside the scope of Gibraltar Customs Duty, and exported services fall outside the scope of Gibraltar Income Tax and Purchase Duty. A supplier of offshore BIM/CAD services may substantiate zero tax treatment by demonstrating that the services are performed on behalf of and delivered to a non-resident recipient, that consideration is received in foreign currency or via international banking channels, and that the entity has no Gibraltar permanent establishment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Gibraltar electronic export submission or Single Administrative Document) — required for tangible goods only
Commercial Invoice and executed Statement of Work for engineering CAD/BIM services
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill or electronic proof of delivery — for tangible goods only
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 credit evidence showing receipt of export proceeds
Certificate of Non-Residence or a technical memorandum confirming the absence of a Gibraltar permanent establishment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Gibraltar imposes penalties for fraudulent customs declarations or materially false export substantiation, including fines of up to GBP 50,000 per declaration, forfeiture of goods, and criminal liability for directors or service providers. Where a purported export transaction is recharacterised as a domestic supply or as generating Gibraltar-source income, the general anti-abuse rule allows the Taxation Office to claw back unpaid tax plus interest and a surcharge of up to 100%; assessments may be issued retrospectively for a six-year period, extended to ten years in cases of deliberate non-disclosure.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No central bank of Gibraltar; the monetary anchor is HM Treasury of the United Kingdom / Bank of England, with banking conduct and AML supervision under the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current and capital accounts. The Gibraltar pound (GIP) is pegged at par to pound sterling and is redeemable at parity with UK sterling. There are no exchange controls restricting current-account trade settlement, dividend distributions, loan repayments, or capital repatriation for a Bermuda Exempted Company operated from Gibraltar. Profit remittance hurdles are limited to normal corporate governance and tax-residency evidence; no Gibraltar withholding tax applies to non-resident shareholders on dividends or royalties, provided no Gibraltar-source income is attributed to a Gibraltar permanent establishment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Gibraltar has no statutory export-proceeds surrender regime, and there is no mandatory conversion requirement for service export receipts. BIM/structural drafting and civil-infrastructure CAD consultancy are classified as services under ISIC 7110, therefore all export invoices may be retained in the invoiced currency, typically GBP or USD or EUR, with no forced conversion or repatriation deadline.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. Offshore digital EMI accounts cannot serve as the primary escrow or treasury clearing rail for a Gibraltar-domiciled corporate entity, because GFSC-regulated banks require licensed banking counterparties for capital escrow and settlement accounts. A Gibraltar-licensed e-money institution or a UK-authorized EMI with Gibraltar passported permission may provide operational float and supplier-disbursement accounts, but such accounts are not viable for tier-1 capital injections or large trade settlements. Wise and similar fintech rails are acceptable only for low-value operational disbursements and cannot substitute for SWIFT clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: GFSC AML regulations do not impose a blanket face-to-face attendance requirement for all account openings. However, licensed Gibraltar banks typically mandate a live video interview with every authorised signatory and beneficial owner. For a Bermuda Exempted Company with non-resident directors and no substantive physical office, banks require a board resolution, certificate of incumbency, original passport and proof-of-address for all directors/UBOs, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, and a certified corporate register excerpt. A physical visit to Gibraltar is strongly recommended for initial onboarding to expedite completion of enhanced due diligence, but full remote onboarding is possible if the bank accepts electronic identity verification through a GFSC-approved third-party provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Gibraltar Economic Substance Act notification and substance return confirming that the company is tax-resident outside Gibraltar; Bermuda tax exemption certificate; registered office/registered agent letter; management agreement demonstrating that core BIM engineering services are performed in Bermuda or another substantive jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear underlying commercial purpose of CAD/BIM service company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master service agreement with civil-infrastructure clients; detailed scopes of work for structural drafting and BIM coordination; prior invoice/payment evidence; project references for highways, utilities, or buildings; procedural explanation of the BIM/CAD outsourcing workflow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds from high-risk or ambiguous jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements of the injecting shareholder; legal source-of-wealth declaration; audited financial statements or certified management accounts of the shareholder; evidence of corporate earnings provenance; confirmation that the injected capital is not derived from proceeds of crime or sanctions evasion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential sanctions exposure in civil infrastructure procurement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated sanctions screening report on all counterparties and project financing sources; end-user declarations for any imported specialised CAD hardware/software; OFAC/UK-OFSI negative-news search results; contractual IP-compliance and export-control clauses.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: SWIFT MT103/T103 wire transfers are the primary compliant routing for inbound capital injection from the Bermuda parent or shareholders into the Gibraltar GIP/GBP account. The wire purpose description must state 'Intercompany capital injection for BIM engineering services working capital' to avoid being misclassified as trade proceeds. Banks require the underlying shareholding structure, board resolution for the capital contribution, and a completed source-of-funds form. For GIP-denominated injections, sterling funds are converted at par with no FX cost. Large injections should be settled via CHAPS or a same-day SWIFT transfer to the bank's clearing account to ensure value-dated availability. The bank will issue a credit advice referencing the capital contribution, and the funds are immediately available for licensed disbursements once KYC/onboarding is completed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for civil-infrastructure BIM/CAD service delivery are executed either by SWIFT MT103 for supplier invoices and subcontractor payments, or by commercial letter of credit through SWIFT MT700 where the transaction involves physical procurement of hardware, software licences, or engineering equipment. The preferred clearing rail is GBP/HKD via SWIFT for Hong Kong or Singaporean CAD subcontractors, and GBP/USD via SWIFT for US cloud rendering and BIM server costs. Commercial LCs are used only for large capital equipment purchases tied to infrastructure projects. All outbound payments must be covered by a matching inbound invoice, disbursement instruction, and internal expenditure approval; SEPA EUR transfers may be used for EU suppliers. Gibraltar clearing does not impose exchange controls or prior approval for these disbursements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forwards with a Gibraltar or UK bank with spot and forward dates against GBP
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currencies used by infrastructure contractors
Cross-currency swaps between GIP/GBP and USD for long-term BIM project receivables
FX options and zero-cost collars for managing contingent bid/cost exposure
Natural hedging via multicurrency accounts and matched invoicing in USD, EUR, or GBP

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Gibraltar imposes a flat corporate income tax rate of 12.5% under the Income Tax Act 2010. A Bermuda Exempted Company that elects Qualifying Company (QC) status under section 13 is treated as a non-resident for tax purposes and is thereby exempt from Gibraltar tax on all non-Gibraltar-source profits, which covers the offshore CAD/BIM engineering fees of the ISIC 7110 scope. No capital gains tax, no value added tax, no annual wealth tax, and no dividend withholding tax apply to a qualifying exempted company. Preferential treatment includes 100% capital allowances on software and computer-aided design equipment, deductibility of certified pension contributions, and the pure equity holding exemption from the Economic Substance Regulations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Gibraltar Company Income Tax Return (Form CT-1) filed through the Gibraltar Income Tax Office GIBTAX electronic filing portal; paper filing is disabled for non-resident qualifying entities and for all entities whose corporate seat is a Gibraltar-registered exempted company.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return is due within 9 months after the end of the chargeable (accounting) period. For an accounting period ending 31 December, the final filing and payment date is 30 September of the following year; for a 30 June year-end, the deadline is 31 March of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Gibraltar company registration number, and Income Tax Office reference number of the Bermuda Exempted Company as registered in Gibraltar.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the exact legal name 'BM_EXEMPTED_CO' and the Gibraltar IX-number; attach the current Qualifying Company certificate and state the exemption class claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commencement and cessation dates of the accounting period covered by the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare a twelve-month GAPP-compliant accounting period; a shortened first period is permitted but the Qualifying Company election must remain in force for the entire period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of total assessable profits before deductions, separately identifying Gibraltar-source trading income and foreign-source BIM/CAD engineering fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 'NIL' for Gibraltar-source income and disclose all foreign-source CAD/BIM revenue in the supplementary schedule; claim the non-resident exclusion to remove such fees from assessable statutory profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Pension contributions, rent, employee costs, software amortisation, and capital allowances on design hardware and BIM infrastructure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only activities performed by the Gibraltar-registered branch and its employees generate deductible expenditure; costs incurred outside Gibraltar are non-deductible for a Qualifying Company and must be eliminated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory tax computation applying the 12.5% Gibraltar corporate rate to the adjusted profits shown in Box 3.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the nil-rate recomputation for the non-resident Qualifying Company; foreign tax credits and treaty credits available under an applicable DTA may be set off at this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Transfer Pricing and ESR Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Endorsement that all inter-company transactions conform to the arm's-length principle and that the company satisfies the Gibraltar Economic Substance test unless exempt as a pure equity holding entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select the 'pure equity holding exempt' box only if the entity holds no commercial trading activity; otherwise attach the transfer pricing Local File table and the ESR employee and expenditure disclosures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signature of the director and of the Gibraltar-resident approved tax agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident exempted company must file through its Gibraltar tax agent; the agent must confirm the registered office is a physical office, not a virtual shell, and must validate the Qualifying Company status.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fixed penalty of GIP 150 plus GIP 60 per day thereafter, capped at GIP 5,000; late payment interest accrues at 1.5% per month and a tax-geared penalty of up to 100% of the unpaid tax applies, rising to 200% for deliberate concealment. Separate ESR notification failures attract a GIP 10,000 penalty plus daily penalties of GIP 1,000 for continued non-compliance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — Gibraltar imposes no statutory withholding tax on dividends paid by a Gibraltar-resident company, including a Bermuda Exempted Company, to non-resident shareholders. The nil rate is final and requires no prior tax authority approval.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Gibraltar maintains double taxation arrangements with the United Kingdom, Malta, Hong Kong, and Israel. To invoke treaty relief: (1) obtain an annual Gibraltar Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the Income Tax Office confirming Qualifying Company or ordinary resident status; (2) deliver the certified TRC or e-TRC code to the source-state payer, bank, or tax authority before the payment date; (3) file the applicable claim form, including the UK-Gibraltar arrangement claim, with HMRC where UK-source income is involved; and (4) retain board minutes, payroll records, lease agreements, and project contracts demonstrating that control and substance are actually exercised in Gibraltar. A Qualifying Company cannot claim UK relief where HMRC establishes central management and control in the UK.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Gibraltar statutory rate: 0% on outbound royalties and 0% on debt interest paid to non-residents. Under the UK-Gibraltar arrangements, royalties and interest paid to a UK-resident beneficial owner are also 0% provided the recipient conducts substantive activity and the amounts are arm's-length. Under the Malta, Hong Kong, and Israel DTAs, interest is generally 0% and royalties range from 0% to 5% depending on the intellectual property character and the beneficial ownership test.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory contemporaneous Local File documentation is required where aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceed GIP 1,000,000 per chargeable period; a Master File is required where the multinational group's global consolidated turnover exceeds €750,000,000 (OECD-aligned threshold). Below the Local File threshold, a retained transfer pricing policy with a functional analysis and gross margin study is compulsory for audit readiness. All TP documentation must be filed within 30 days of the Income Tax Office request.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Gibraltar's Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), enacted under the Income Tax (Economic Substance) rules, apply to companies conducting a relevant activity. ISIC 7110 offshore BIM/structural drafting services constitute a 'service centre business' when rendered to group companies or connected parties. The entity must maintain: (I) a physical registered office and actual premises in Gibraltar; (II) at least one director and one employee exercising independent decision-making in Gibraltar, with staffing proportionate to the revenue; and (III) annual operating expenditure in Gibraltar of between GIP 100,000 and GIP 500,000 depending on the volume of activities. A pure equity holding entity with no commercial service activity is fully exempt. Failure to satisfy the test causes reassessment of the entire revenue at 12.5% and triggers the ESR penalty regime.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: UK Tax Evasion — Central Management and Control Misdeclaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Directors of the Gibraltar-registered Bermuda Exempted Company take strategic decisions, negotiate engineering contracts, and direct BIM operations from London or elsewhere in the UK while the entity declares itself non-resident in Gibraltar and omits the profits from UK corporation tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: HMRC applies the central management and control test to reclassify the entity as UK-resident; all worldwide profits, including the Gibraltar-excluded offshore CAD/BIM revenue, are reassessed at the UK 19% corporation tax rate with interest; deliberate non-disclosure penalties up to 100% of tax avoided and criminal prosecution under the Fraud Act 2006 and CTA 2010 false-statement provisions carry fines and imprisonment up to 7 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for restitution of unpaid group tax; UK and Gibraltar courts may issue disqualification orders up to 15 years, travel bans, and custodial sentences of up to 7 years for dishonestly filing misleading CT-1 declarations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Gibraltar Shell-Company and ESR Substance Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a mailbox-only registered office in Gibraltar, exploiting the Bermuda Exempted Company label as a pure conduit, carrying no local payroll, and failing to file ESR category notifications while all design services are performed by remote overseas subcontractors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Gibraltar Companies Registry and Income Tax Office impose financial penalties up to GIP 200,000 on first offence, daily penalties of GIP 1,000 for continued infringement, compulsory strike-off of the company, revocation of Qualifying Company status, and retrospective taxation at 12.5% on the gross infrastructure design revenues of the preceding six years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the resultant unpaid tax through civil restitution orders, ban from acting as a director for 10 years, travel bans preventing departure from Gibraltar during investigation, and exclusion from financial services sectors in Gibraltar, Jersey, and the Isle of Man.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Profit Shifting in CAD-BIM Outsourcing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Gibraltar entity invoices civil infrastructure clients at artificially reduced margins while diverting the residual profit through inter-company royalties for BIM technology or software licences to a zero-tax Bermuda parent, violating the arm's-length principle and shifting taxable substance away from the UK.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Gibraltar transfer pricing audit re-determines an arm's-length net contribution margin of 18-25%; the resulting profit is taxed at 12.5% in Gibraltar or 19% in the UK through the joint competent-authority procedure, plus late-payment interest; mispricing penalties up to 200% of the adjustment apply and DTA relief on related-party royalties is denied where economic substance fails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing non-arm's-length agreements face penal surcharges, disqualification under the Gibraltar Companies Act, personal civil liability for the group's lost tax, and joint and several liability in cross-border avoidance proceedings initiated by HMRC and the Gibraltar Income Tax Office.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Economic Crime Failure on Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Funding the Gibraltar exempted company through Wire Transfer and Wise rails from engineering counterparties without conducting sufficient client due diligence, transaction monitoring, or PEP screening, and using circular invoicing arrangements to conceal treasury flows and the ultimate beneficial owners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Gibraltar Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 and AML/CTF regulations, fines up to GIP 10,000,000 and custodial penalties up to 14 years for money laundering by arrangement apply; the Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit may freeze accounts, revoke the company's registration, and list the entity on the sanctions register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the Money Laundering Reporting Officer are individually criminally liable; the Crown may obtain confiscation orders, travel bans, asset seizure, and a permanent bar from Gibraltar banking infrastructure; extradition to the UK is available where the laundered funds enter the UK financial system.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Repatriation and Earnings Stripping — Disguised Distributions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using excessive 'BIM design software licensing' fees or management charges denominated at the place of intellectual property residence to strip profits out of Gibraltar or the UK while claiming the zero-rate dividend withholding status and DTA relief on payments that are economically distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Gibraltar re-characterises the excessive royalties as distributions, adding 12.5% corporate tax and prejudicial interest; HMRC may invoke the diverted profits tax at 25% on the artificial offshore arrangement; penalties for fraudulent withholding claims reach 100% of the sums, and an anti-avoidance ruling invalidates the entire structure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors responsible for the re-characterised distributions are personally liable for the shortfall in UK withholding tax deductions, subject to civil restitution, monthly travel restriction notices, and extradition proceedings between Gibraltar and the UK in severe circumstances.
